items.title: A prime ideal containing a product of two ideals contains one of them
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a prime ideal p containing a product IJ of two ideals contains at least one of the factors (statement lines 2767-2771). The proof is a one-step contradiction: witnesses outside p are chosen in each ideal, their product lies in the product and therefore in p, and primality forces one factor to have been in p after all (proof lines 2773-2778). What the short argument uses is that the product IJ lies inside the ideal generated by it, and that primality is available in element-wise form, which is what makes the choice of witnesses worthwhile; the author writes out the whole contradiction. H2.
